person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: method
span.quote: In this paper, we present a network and training strategy that relies on the strong use of data augmentation to use the available annotated samples more efficiently.

span.label: biomedical image segmentation
span.quote: However, in many visual tasks, especially in biomedical image processing, the desired output should include localization, i.e., a class label is supposed to be assigned to each pixel.

span.label: system-or-tool-building
span.quote: We provide the full Caffe[6]-based implementation and the trained networks4.

span.label: Because convolutions are unpadded, border pixels are lost at every layer and feature maps must be cropped before concatenation.
span.quote: The cropping is necessary due to the loss of border pixels in every convolution.

span.label: Without the overlap-tile strategy the resolution the network can handle is bounded by GPU memory.
span.quote: This tiling strategy is important to apply the network to large images, since otherwise the resolution would be limited by the GPU memory.

span.label: Part of what the network is trained to detect is inserted by the authors: the separation borders between touching cells are synthesised, not annotated.
span.quote: and to force the network to learn the small separation borders that we introduce between touching cells (See Figure 3c and d). The separation border is computed using morphological operations

span.label: How heavily those borders count is set by two chosen constants in the loss.
span.quote: In our experiments we set w0 = 10 and σ ≈ 5 pixels

span.label: The invariances the network has are the ones the augmentation supplied, and the paper says the corpus never contained them.
span.quote: This allows the network to learn invariance to such deformations, without the need to see these transformations in the annotated image corpus

span.label: convolutional networks applied to biomedical image segmentation
span.quote: outperforms the prior best method (a sliding-window convolutional network) on the ISBI challenge for segmentation of

span.label: the ground truth - PARTLY SYNTHESISED: the annotation is augmented with separation borders computed by morphological operations so that touching instances can be pulled apart, so the target is the annotation plus an artefact of the method
span.quote: We pre-compute the weight map for each ground truth segmentation to compensate the different frequency of pixels from a certain class in the training data set, and to force the network to learn the small separation borders that we introduce between touching cells (See Figure 3c and d). The separation border is computed using morphological operations

span.label: very few images - AS THIRTY, AND THEN AS PATCHES: the electron-microscopy training set is 30 images, and the paper notes that in patches the training data is much larger than the image count suggests
span.quote: The training data is a set of 30 images (512x512 pixels) from serial section transmission electron microscopy of the Drosophila first instar larva ventral nerve cord

span.label: invariance - AS A PROPERTY OF THE AUGMENTATION: what the network is invariant to is what was applied to the training images, not what was observed in the microscopy
span.quote: As for our tasks there is very little training data available, we use excessive data augmentation by applying elastic deformations to the available training images

span.quote: In this paper, we build upon a more elegant architecture, the so-called “fully convolutional network” [9].

span.label: extends → the fully convolutional network of Long et al. [9]
span.quote: We modify and extend this architecture such that it works with very few training images and yields more precise segmentations; see Figure 1.
